subject: Residency commitment: keystore provenance + PrivateLink access assertion
messages:
From: Sanjay Patel <sanjay@veridian-health.com>
To: grace_oconnor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Cc: Veridian Legal <legalops@veridian-health.com>
Date: 2026-05-20 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Residency + keystore provenance for PrivateLink pilot

Hi Grace,

Thanks again for the call this morning. As we prep our SOC 2+SIG intake for the PrivateLink pilot, Veridian needs two quick confirmations so we can close the architecture review with InfoSec: 1) a short provenance list for operator keystores used for EU/US partitioned deployments (who generated keys, where they are stored, rotation cadence), and 2) a drawing or simple assertion that when our private endpoint is used traffic egress for inference never leaves the US-hosted subnet (we'll accept an ops-runbook excerpt or diagram).

Can you send the keystore inventory and the PrivateLink topology diagram (even an annotated PNG) that we can drop into our CAIQ/SIG package? We're trying to avoid a long artifact request cycle. If you can also point to any SIG control statements that cover key custody and peering egress controls that would be ideal.

Sanjay
Director, InfoSec Operations
Veridian Health

Attachments: none

From: grace_oconnor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
To: Sanjay Patel <sanjay@veridian-health.com>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, rishi_malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-05-20 10:01:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Residency + keystore provenance for PrivateLink pilot

Sanjay — thanks for the clear ask. Looping in Marissa (Customer Success) and Rishi (Security/Onboarding) so we can get the minimum-viable packet to you today.

Plan: Marissa will attach the PrivateLink topology and a short runbook excerpt; Rishi will produce the keystore provenance CSV (operator, origin, KMS region, rotation cadence) plus SIG control callouts. Grace will consolidate into a 1-page cover note so your team can drop it into the CAIQ.

Quick question — do you want a signed attestation or is a timestamped artifact bundle sufficient for your audit intake?

—Grace
Director, Customer Security
Redwood Inference

From: rishi_malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
To: grace_oconnor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: irene_choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-05-20 14:28:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Residency + keystore provenance for PrivateLink pilot

Team — attaching the artifacts for Veridian. Summary below; full files attached.

--- keystore_inventory_202605.csv (attached) — columns: operator_name, created_by, created_date_utc, kms_region, key_type (HSM/KMS), rotation_days, custody_boundary_notes
Examples: 
  - operator_redwood_ops, redwood-kms-team, 2024-10-03T02:12:00Z, us-west-2, KMS, 90, keys stored in customer partitioned keystore; operator access via sealed operator role
  - operator-dedicated, vendor-onprem, 2023-07-11T12:00:00Z, us-east-1, HSM, 365, on-prem HSM used for dedicated installations (air-gapped when requested)

--- privatelink_topology_v2.png (attached) — annotated: shows PrivateLink endpoint in the customer's VPC, traffic flow constrained to US-only egress for the inference path, and fallback routing to our hosted US cluster only if customer endpoint fails. Diagram notes list the routing ACLs and peering policy that prevent cross-region egress.

--- redwood_sig_subset.pdf (attached) — excerpts from our SIG responses pointing at control mappings: CR.2 (key management), NET.1 (network segregation), and TRN.3 (transport encryption). Each excerpt references the corresponding SOC2 control and the artifact in our compliance repo.

Operational clarifications for Veridian: 1) When a PrivateLink is provisioned into a US-only tenant we provision dedicated routing tables that do not include cross-region NAT or transit gateways; 2) Key material that protects customer encryption at rest is anchored in regional KMS or customer-managed HSMs per contract; 3) We support key rotation windows and offer an HSM escrow mechanism for on-prem/dedicated installs.

Irene, could you confirm the wording on the runbook snippet we'll share in the cover note? Marissa — please package these three files and I will sign off on provenance statements before we send to Veridian.

-rishi
Security Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Sanjay Patel <sanjay@veridian-health.com>
Cc: grace_oconnor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>, rishi_malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, irene_choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-05-21 16:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Residency + keystore provenance for PrivateLink pilot

Sanjay / Veridian team — attaching the packet referenced below. Quick cover note: these artifacts are the minimal set we provide for pilot onboarding; if you'd like an executed attestation on Redwoods letterhead we can arrange a countersigned PDF (legal ops prefer a 48-hour turnaround).

Attached: privatelink_topology_v2.png; keystore_inventory_202605.csv; redwood_sig_subset.pdf

Key bullets for your CAIQ/SIG intake:
- Traffic path: customer->PrivateLink->regional inference pool (US) — no cross-region hops unless explicitly requested in contract.
- Key custody: regional KMS by default; HSM for Dedicated/On-prem; operator access limited and auditable.
- Rotation: default 90-day rotation for KMS keys; 365-day for custodian HSM keys unless customer requests stricter cadence.

Next steps: if this is sufficient, confirm and we'll mark HubSpot VS-19427 as "Docs Delivered". If you need a countersigned attestation, flag Legal and we'll route the request.

Thanks — Marissa
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
